- Scope: The guide covers edge computing, IoT, machine learning in networking, blockchain, and AI-driven network management, with protocol-level details (IPsec AH/ESP) and a rapid revision matrix summarizing core concepts, advantages, and challenges.

- IPsec AH: RFC 4302; provides data-origin authentication, integrity, and anti-replay protection. Crucial limitation — no encryption/confidentiality (payload remains plaintext). Key AH header fields: Next Header, Payload Length, Reserved, SPI, Sequence Number, and Integrity Check Value (ICV).

- IPsec ESP: Header (unencrypted) contains SPI and Sequence Number; Payload & Trailer are encrypted (payload data, padding, pad length, next header); ESP Auth contains an ICV (HMAC) covering header, payload and trailer. ESP does not authenticate the outer IP header (allows NAT traversal via UDP port 4500).

- Edge vs Cloud (concise comparison): Edge processes near data source with ultra-low latency (1–10 ms), lower bandwidth use, distributed scaling, lower Internet dependency and higher data privacy; Cloud is centralized with higher latency (50–250+ ms), higher bandwidth consumption, centralized scaling, and greater WAN dependency.

- Blockchain & Smart Contracts: Uses PKI/digital signatures for trust. Smart contracts enable self-executing policies for dynamic SLAs, automated bandwidth trading, and dynamic spectrum leasing without trusted intermediaries. Blockchain offers tamper-proof trust but faces high latency and scalability bottlenecks.

- AI for Network Management: Modernizes the FCAPS framework toward closed-loop, zero-touch control and self-healing networks, improving resilience; key challenges include model explainability, data quality, and integration complexity with legacy systems.

- Rapid revision highlights: Edge — ultra-low latency but resource constraints; IoT — ubiquitous sensing with protocol fragmentation and security risks; ML — adaptive decision-making with explainability/data-quality issues; Blockchain — decentralized trust with scalability/latency limits; AI network management — self-healing but integration complexity.
